cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Use the Proper Title
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. At the staff barbecue, introduce me as Director Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing everyone by first name. Even the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Then give me a separate introduction when I welcome the staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. You offered to serve burgers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce the burger service: 'Director Patel will serve you.' I'd like them to hear who's making this gesture.

mechanism: A copies a misunderstood status custom and asks B to turn it into an actual public courtesy acknowledging A standing.
confusable: D51 seeks apology for disrespect; D57 requests recognition without needing a prior offense.
comparison: Public barbecue introduction versus seating title on a place card.
seedUse: Use service duty and limited display room as real constraints; do not merely add pompous vocabulary.
